levels.0: assembly: entrypoints and wiring allowed to reference any layer
levels.1: foundation services: platform capabilities and operations domains
levels.2: window containers and the embedded browser domain

notes: A file with no matching prefix has no layer constraint; the check reports mapped coverage so gaps stay visible.
Level 0 files are exempt from layer rules in both directions.
Level 2 entries may declare domain and allowedDomains; level 2 to level 2 edges are only allowed when the target domain is listed.
The operations domain (updates, diagnostics) stays physically in place; prefixes record its level only.
electron/window-factory/ now only holds app-icon.ts at level 1; the browser domain moved to electron/browser/.

electron/modules/plugins/ is level 3: every built-in plugin keeps its wiring and plugin-owned implementations in one subdirectory. The plugin framework files at the top of electron/modules/ stay unconstrained until the shared-base split ends their inversion.

L1 window, security and diagnostics services read browser data through electron/platform/browser-port.ts; application-main installs the browser implementations before any window is created, so reads never reach into electron/browser/ directly.
Profile and preset persistence serve both settings UI and browser identities; they live in the browser domain and are exposed to L1 through the browser port.
